questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The fact that I had never been there before and that it seemed to have lots of beautiful nature. Also the fact that it was an English speaking country, as I thought this would make it easier to connect with people.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall, I am very glad that I went on the exchange as I have had some great experiences traveling around the country and experiencing the culture. However, I experienced a lot of difficulties leading up to the exchange; for instance with having my courses pre-approved by KU and receiving wrongful information and documentation from KU. Altogether, this meant that the months leading up to the exchange were pretty stressful for me. Of course this was not a part of my exchange per se, but it nonetheless affected my overall experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I did find the whole proces of getting admitted into the courses I needed etc. quite confusing and VUW were often slow in responding to my e-mails. However, when I arrived and was able to visit the Student Administration Office in person, they were very keen to help me out.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any assistance per se, besides from the help I received when visiting the Student Administration Office and the information I got during the orientation week.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The staff were definitely very keen to help, though they were sometimes a bit hard to get in touch with. The orientation week was not all that good in my opinion; the program was the same for all students (international students, exchange students, undergraduate students and graduate students) and thus it was not all that relevant for me as an exchange student.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing through Facebook (there are a number of Facebook pages for finding flatmates in Wellington that are quite helpful). It was easy enough to find somewhere, but finding a place that is both affordable, not too far away from campus and in good condition is quite hard.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: As mentioned above, finding a place that is affordable without it being far away from campus/the city and not being very cold during winter (houses are generally not very well isolated in Wellington, resulting in cold/damp/mould infested houses, especially during winter) is quite hard.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: In spite of the fact that I lived a bit outside of the city, living off campus allowed me to live with 3 kiwis; this was a great opportunity to learn about the culture, and (as Kiwis generally are) they were very kind and helpful and overall nice to live with.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As I only had a limited number of courses pre-approved by KU, I was not very flexible with the courses I could take at VUW. Thus, I found the whole process quite stressful as the course registration process does not finish at VUW until the beginning of the semester, meaning that I was unsure of whether or not I could actually get the courses I needed until the last minute.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I applied for courses in an online portal and after some time was admitted into a number of courses. In contrast to at KU, at VUW you do not submit different "course wishes" for the same course, you are simply admitted into all the courses you applied for with space and then you drop the courses you don't want to take.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can get help by contacting your "Student Success Adviser". I also recommend contacting the lecturers of the courses you are interested in taking, they are very helpful in answering questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I registered for 2/3 of the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Definitely contacting the lecturers of the courses you are interested in taking if you have any course specific questions.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I wouldn't say that the courses were harder than courses at KU, but they certainly required a lot more work during the course period, i.e. due to having a lot of group work, weekly assignments, oral presentations etc.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: All my classes at VUW were discussion based and quite small with around 15 people or less. The style of teaching varied quite a lot between the classes; some of them involved lots of group work, others involved more full class discussions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
PSYC434 - Conduction Research across Cultures
PSYC412 - The Psychology of Criminal Conduct
PSYC437 - Advanced Human Memory

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend PSYC412 (The Psychology of Criminal Psychology) as the classes were very interesting and quite thought provoking. Also, the lecturers were very engaging and knowledgeable.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not expect food and housing to be quite as expensive as it was.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is very expensive, especially vegetables and fresh food in general (a "cheap" cucumber would cost $6!). Also, housing is expensive. Coffee is probably the only thing that is cheaper in NZ than in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were quite a lot of clubs and athletic and social opportunities; everything from international clubs to football clubs etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I actually did not engage in any non-academic activities at VUW.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There is so much to see in New Zealand! I recommend going tramping at the Tongariro Crossing, taking the train to Auckland from Wellington (goes through beautiful scenery), going on a whale trip in beautiful Kaikoura and visiting Wanaka.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy; kiwis are quite like Danes and generally very kind and open.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Joining clubs or going to the orientation week. Since I was at the graduate level, people were generally quite "set" socially, i.e. not all that open to meeting new people at uni. Nonetheless, people were very friendly!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any cultural differences to be challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are genuinely so kind and helpful in New Zealand and I always felt very safe traveling around in the country.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Pack warm clothes! Wellington quite often gets cold, windy and wet.
2. Pack you hiking boots; there is so much beautiful nature to explore.
3. Save up enough money; living costs in NZ are high.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just that I would really recommend going on exchange in spite of all the hard work with applying, getting scholarships etc. - it is so worth it!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Definitely traveling around. New Zealand is such a beautiful country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Probably the fact that uni was so "hands on" and required so much work; I had expected it to be more easy going, but I had a lot of assignments, presentations etc. and was required to participate in all my courses. I had hoped for uni to be a bit more "lose" so I could go on more spontaneous trips etc.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
